content_groups.group_title: ❌ Trap 6: Diagnosing from an inadequate image

blocks.text: Always comment on technical adequacy when relevant.
A potassium of 7 mmol/L or severe hypoglycaemia is not merely an abnormal laboratory result.
A clinical emergency requiring prompt action.
I — Identify D — Describe I — Interpret D — Diagnose N — Next step
When handed any investigation, immediately ask:

☐ What is it? ☐ Is it technically adequate? ☐ What do I see? ☐ What is abnormal? ☐ What does it mean? ☐ What is the likely diagnosis? ☐ What are the important differentials? ☐ Is this an emergency? ☐ What do I do next?

“This is a [name of investigation] from a [age]-year-old child. The key findings are [describe abnormalities]. These findings are consistent with [interpretation]. In the clinical context, the most likely diagnosis is [diagnosis], although [important differential] should be considered. I would assess the child's clinical stability immediately, correlate the result with the clinical findings and proceed with [next investigation/management].”
That structure works for blood tests, urine, CSF, ECG and imaging.
